moon.title: Gravity
moon.text: The Moon pulls at 0.17 g. Walking gait, wheel loads, sinkage and dust flight all change.
moon.lab: Gravity offload (NASA JSC ARGOS), parabolic flights

moon.title: Hard vacuum
moon.text: No air means no convection and no wind. Heat moves only by radiation and contact.
moon.lab: Thermal-vacuum chambers (NASA JSC Chamber A, GRC)

moon.title: Radiation
moon.text: No magnetic field or atmosphere. Solar particles and cosmic rays reach the ground.
moon.lab: Beam facilities (NASA Space Radiation Lab, Brookhaven)

moon.title: Permanently shadowed cold
moon.text: Crater floors stay below ~100 K. Earth's coldest ground is ~180 K.

moon.title: Grazing light
moon.text: At the south pole the Sun never climbs above ~2°. High-latitude Earth gives low sun for part of the year, with a blue sky that fills shadows.

moon.title: Regolith and dust
moon.text: Lunar dust is sharp, glassy and electrostatically charged. Earth soils are weathered and damp; volcanic ash is the closest match.
moon.lab: Simulant bins (LHS-1, LMS-1) with UV charging

mars.title: Thin CO₂ air
mars.text: Surface pressure is ~0.6 kPa of CO₂. Earth's highest ground is still ~50 kPa of nitrogen and oxygen.
mars.lab: Mars environment chambers (NASA Ames Mars Wind Tunnel, Aarhus)

mars.title: Radiation and UV
mars.text: No global magnetic field and no ozone. Ultraviolet sterilises the surface.

mars.title: Cold and swing
mars.text: Ground swings ~90 K a day around a mean near −60 °C. Earth's cold deserts match the mean, not the swing.

mars.title: Oxidising soil
mars.text: Perchlorate-rich, oxidising soils. Atacama and the Dry Valleys hold perchlorate at lower levels.

mars.title: Global dust
mars.text: Planet-wide dust storms coat panels and optics for weeks.
